svg.title: Voltage sag: the battery dips under load
svg.desc: Animated graph. The battery voltage line is drawn left to right above a strip showing current. Each time current flows, the battery volts dip. In the first, smaller burst the dip stays above the dashed line where full stick needs about 10 V, so the SPARKs make up for it. In the second burst, drawing hard with all four drive motors accelerating, it sags below 10 V; that stretch fills in red: not enough volts left, so the robot is slower than asked. A red line marks about 6.75 V, below which a roboRIO 2 browns out and cuts the motors; SystemCore has its own level.
svg.text: Voltage sag: the battery dips under load
The battery voltage drops while current flows.
brownout: a roboRIO 2 cuts the motors (SystemCore: its own level)
drawing hard: all four drive motors accelerating
YAGSL's voltage compensation at 12 V means the same gains do the same
thing on a full battery or a tired one, until the battery sags below what is
asked. Then nothing can push harder. Tests refuse to start on a low battery.
